newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Pac property unit kills float plan.
newsitem.headline: First Pac property unit kills float plan.

text.p: Conglomerate First Pacific Co Ltd's property unit First Pacific Davies has scrapped plans to list this year after a proposed merger with a property management company fell through, the South China Morning Post said on Sunday.
But it did not rule out a future float in Hong Kong that would finance corporate acquisitions and raise its profile, the daily quoted the unit's managing director Godfrey Blott as saying.
Officials from the group were not available for comment.

"We no longer intend to pursue the flotation of First Pacific Daives this year, because concurrent with the float, we had intended to merge it with another company and then list," Blott said, adding that: "The merger fell through."

The property agency and consultancy was "in the process of looking at complementary business to acquire", the newspaper quoted the parent group's corporate communications vice president Derek Murphy as saying.
First Pacific Davies was considering acquiring some property agencies in Hong Kong this year as well as expanding in Australia, the newspaper said.
